properties.property: Facilitates explicit computation of antiderivatives, Taylor series expansions, inverse Z-transforms, and inverse Laplace transforms
properties.why: Decomposing a complex rational function into fractions with simpler denominators enables term-by-term integration or transformation

properties.property: Component numerators A_i(x) are given by the Taylor polynomials of P(x)/Q_i(x) of order \nu_i - 1 at \lambda_i
properties.why: P(x)/Q_i(x) equals A_i(x) + O((x - \lambda_i)^{\nu_i}) as x approaches \lambda_i

properties.property: For simple poles (\nu_i = 1), decomposition coefficients are the residues given by P(z_i)/Q'(z_i)
properties.why: Multiplying the decomposition by (z - z_i) and taking the limit as z approaches z_i isolates P(z_i)/Q'(z_i)

properties.property: Coefficients can be evaluated by multiplying by denominator factors and taking limits or evaluating derivatives
properties.why: Multiplying by a factor clears the denominator for that component while causing terms containing the factor to vanish at the pole

properties.property: The partial fraction concept extends to other integral domains such as the ring of integers
properties.why: Prime numbers take the role of irreducible denominators in integral domains

assumptions.assumption: Strictly proper rational fraction: deg(P) < deg(Q)
assumptions.breaks_when: deg(P) >= deg(Q), requiring polynomial long division first to separate out a non-zero polynomial quotient

assumptions.assumption: The denominator Q(x) is factored into powers of linear factors (x - \lambda_j)^{\nu_j}
assumptions.breaks_when: Roots \lambda_j cannot be found or factoring is not performed over the base field

assumptions.assumption: The numerator and denominator are polynomials
assumptions.breaks_when: The expression contains non-polynomial, fractional power, or transcendental functions

failure_modes.mode: Omission of polynomial long division for improper fractions
failure_modes.signature: Degrees of partial fraction terms fail to account for the polynomial part, leading to inconsistent coefficient equations
failure_modes.cause: Applying the proper partial fraction template directly when deg(P) >= deg(Q)

failure_modes.mode: Direct evaluation at poles without clearing denominators or taking limits
failure_modes.signature: Division by zero or indeterminate 0/0 expressions
failure_modes.cause: Evaluating the original fraction at roots of the denominator where it is undefined

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so partial_fractions is recorded as a definition
